key_insight: Greedy decoding is not fully deterministic across numeric precision: the same prompt/model can diverge between BF16 and FP16 because tiny logit-margins get flipped by accumulated numerical error.
engineering_relevance: Inference systems that mix precisions can change LLM outputs, so precision policy, batch size, and selective high-precision recomputation matter for reliability in deployed serving stacks.
method: Measured cross-precision output divergence for 6 LLMs across 3 benchmarks on identical hardware.
Analyzed error propagation and found top-2 logit margin at the LM head is the main predictor of flip vs. no-flip outcomes.
Evaluated selective FP32 LM-head recomputation as a low-overhead mitigation.
evidence_signal: Across six models (1.1B–7B, plus 12B characterization) and three benchmarks, 49–100% of prompts diverged between BF16 and FP16; selective FP32 LM-head recomputation improved exact agreement by 22–36 percentage points on A10G with under 4% latency overhead at batch size ≤4.
watch_item: The mitigation is not a universal fix: its benefit fades when body-originated error dominates, especially at batch size ≥8 or under end-to-end FP8.
paper_title: Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant: Cross-Precision Output Divergence in LLM Inference
